Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the fish-control skill and its required references, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace.

I’m also using the workspace’s “read wake visual signals first” skill because this policy must be grounded in both 3D wake views before any architecture change. I’ve now confirmed the fish-control shelf requires those visuals and metrics to precede its primitive references.

The visual evidence separates two failure modes: the strongest sampled controller sustains a coherent, nearly axial reverse-Kármán street and long self-propelled travel, but passes roughly 5L from the target and drifts to the upper boundary; another controller executes a large downward turn, approaches only to 8.17L, then exits the opposite boundary. I’m now tying those trajectories to their exact feedback structures and logged signal scales before selecting the mechanism.

The inherited logs confirm that the current prefill’s response-gated posterior steering failed early (minimum 11.79L), while the differential turn-rate servo is the only architecture that materially changed trajectory semantics (minimum 4.98L and 33.2T survival). Per the structured transfer protocol, I’m consulting the bookshelf now; any source-informed edit will be recorded in the required transfer block.

The selected mechanism is a persistent differential-curvature redirect, not a gain retune. The key defect in the best rollout is structural: measured beat-scale yaw reaches about ±2.6 rad/T while the desired route turn is capped at 0.5 rad/T, so the existing servo lets oscillatory yaw reverse the steering request every half-beat; after 8T, bearing stays negative while the fish continues almost straight near y≈14–15L. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification boundary before touching the candidate, as required.

The single solver candidate is now implemented. It retains the only sampled architecture with long coherent propulsion, but makes persistent normalized lateral target error authoritative over steering sign; yaw feedback is one-sided release only. I’m now distilling the completed-rollout evidence—not the unevaluated new candidate—into durable guidance.
Both required provenance files are materially updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated check-runner now; it will run only the guidance, policy-contract, schema, and edit-boundary checks—no CFD.

The first mandated check exposed a workspace-rendering defect: `README.md` contains the same “copied to guidance” parent marker twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. This predates the candidate and is unrelated to policy content. I’m making the minimal semantic-preserving repair—removing only the duplicate marker—then rerunning the check.

The guidance check now passes. The policy check itself is currently blocked only because `julia` is absent from this shell’s `PATH` (the candidate was not executed and no assertion failed). I’m locating the workspace’s pinned Julia launcher and will rerun the same dry contract check through it; this remains non-CFD.

Dry execution through the pinned Julia runtime now passes for finite actions and reflection symmetry. The deterministic parameter audit also passes: every one of the 11 direct `params.FIELD` references is declared by `target_policy_params`, and the candidate contains no time, route, random, file-I/O, or cylinder dependency. The mandated boundary check has also passed.

Implemented exactly one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): persistent target-signed differential curvature with one-sided yaw-response release.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:42): reusable lesson that beat-scale yaw must not invert persistent route commands.

The bookshelf’s bounded burst-redirect invariant informed the one-sided response gate. All mandated checks passed: guidance materiality, exact Julia policy contract, parameter schema, reflection symmetry, and solver edit boundary. No CFD was run; evaluation remains downstream.

I also removed a duplicated assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md:122), which was preventing the mandated guidance checker from resolving the parent.
